name: System76, Inc.
subcategory: Linux computers, open firmware and open-hardware peripherals
origin_detail: Founded in Denver, Colorado in 2005 by Carl Richell (CEO) and Erik Fetzer (who had registered the domain in 2003) to be a high-quality OEM for GNU/Linux; the first computers shipped with Ubuntu 5.10. Since 2018 it designs and builds Thelio desktops in its own Denver factory; laptops are largely based on ODM designs.
flagship_projects: System76 Open Firmware (coreboot + EDK2 + open EC)
Thelio desktops and Thelio Io board
openness_notes: Hardware column. In 2005 System76 sold computers with a preinstalled open-source OS (Ubuntu) while hardware and firmware were closed: only peripheral parts open (1). It has opened progressively: Pop!_OS (2017), its own desktop environment COSMIC (GPL-3.0-or-later), an open firmware distribution built on coreboot, EDK2 and its own EC firmware, and fully open designs for some in-house hardware: the Launch keyboard (CC-BY-SA-4.0 chassis, GPLv3 KiCad PCB, GPLv2 QMK firmware, OSHWA US001062) and the Thelio Io board (GPL-3.0 KiCad). Its laptops, the bulk of the range, are not open designs. Overall: open firmware/software with mostly closed hardware designs (2), with individual products at level 3.

license_history.note: Year is Thelio's launch with Denver manufacturing; publication date of the hardware repository not verified.

license_history.license: CC-BY-SA-4.0 (Launch chassis), GPL-3.0 (Launch PCB), GPL-2.0 (QMK-based firmware); OSHWA US001062

license_history.note: First alpha August 2024; default desktop in Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS (2025-12-11).

relicensing_events.to: In-house Thelio desktop with open (GPL-3.0) Thelio Io board design
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Accompanied by moving desktop manufacturing to a Denver factory.
Mechanical, electrical, firmware and configurator all published.

risk_events: Laptops depend on ODM (Clevo-type) designs, limiting how open the main product line can be; an in-house 'Virgo' laptop was announced in April 2023
2021-2025: multi-year rewrite of its desktop environment (COSMIC) in Rust; Pop!_OS 24.04 shipped only in December 2025 with COSMIC as default
robustness: Over 20 years of continuous operation as a privately held niche OEM. Its software (Pop!_OS, COSMIC) and firmware are open and could be maintained by others; open-hardware products (Launch, Thelio Io) are fully reproducible, but most laptops rely on closed ODM designs and supply.
physical_science_relevance: Linux workstations and open-firmware laptops are common in research computing; Pop!_OS has been positioned for 'developers, makers, and computer science professionals'.
openness_effect_assessment: System76's openness grew over time rather than shrinking: from reselling Linux PCs (2005) to its own OS (2017), open firmware, an in-house desktop with an open board (2018) and an OSHWA-certified keyboard (2021). Openness is its brand differentiator in a niche Linux market, and it has kept the company independent for two decades, but there is no public evidence that it produced large scale; revenue and headcount are not disclosed.
key_takeaway: System76 is a long-lived US example of an open-software-first hardware company that opened progressively, ending up with open OS, open firmware and some fully open hardware (Launch, OSHWA US001062), while its laptops remain closed ODM designs. Its longevity (since 2005) without disclosed outside funding contrasts with VC-backed peers, though its ownership and finances are not public.

unconfirmed.reason: No official page fetched states 2005. system76.com/about gives no year. The 2026-07-30 blog post (system76.com/blog/post/system76-goes-to-college-a-case-study) says 'over our company's two-decade history' and 'For over 20 years, System76 has supplied Linux computer hardware...', which fits 2005 but is not explicit. system76.com/press returned 404, de.wikipedia.org/wiki/System76 returned 404, and the 2026-11-18 Thelio Prime post gives no year.

Only the cited OSHWA certificate dates the Launch opening. System76's 2021-05-06 industrial-design post does not mention Launch, and system76.com/accessories/launch returned 404. api.github.com shows the system76/launch repo was created 2019-12-05 (licence GPL-3.0), so design files may have been public before the 2021 certification and release. 2021 is defensible as the certification year but was not re-confirmed.
